Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:2: "I am the LORD your God" - blessed be the Omnipresent, and so on - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: My children, I am He who set aside 974 generations before the world was created, and I came and cleaved to you. I am He who set aside the idol-worshipping nations of the earth, and I came and cleaved to you. I am He who set aside the whole idol-worshipping world, and chose you, and called you My children and My servants. I am He of whom it is said (Isaiah 43:10), "before Me no god was formed, and after Me there shall be none" - and I called you My brothers. I am He of whom it is said (ibid. 45:21), "a just God and a Savior, there is none besides Me" - and I equated your name with My great Name, and My great Name with your name. I am He before the world was created, and I am He since the world was created; I am He in this world, and I am He in the World to Come; "I will put to death, and I will bring to life; I have wounded, and I will heal" (Deuteronomy 32:39) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:3: And along these lines, it says in the Mechilta, Parashat Mishpatim (Nezikin 2), on the verse (Exodus 34:23), "three times in the year shall all your males appear before the Master, the LORD, God of Israel" - they say, of blessed memory: but is it not already said (Deuteronomy 16:16), "before the LORD your God"? What then does it teach by saying "the Master, God of Israel"? Rather, upon Israel He unified His Name more specifically. Similarly, "Hear, O Israel, the LORD our God, the LORD is One" (Deuteronomy 6:4) - but is it not already said "the LORD our God"? What then does it teach by saying "the LORD is One"? Rather, upon us He unified His Name more specifically. Similarly (Jeremiah 32:36), "therefore thus says the LORD, God of Israel" - but is it not already said "God of all flesh"? What then does it teach by saying "God of Israel"? Rather, upon Israel He unified His Name more specifically. Similarly (Psalms 50:7), "hear, O My people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against you: God, your God, am I. I will not rebuke you for your sacrifices, or your burnt offerings, which are continually before Me" - I am God to all who come into the world, even though I have unified My Name only upon Israel - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:4: And besides unifying His Name upon Israel, to be called the God of Israel, further, out of His love for them, He caused His Shechinah to rest among them. And so Rabbi Tanchuma explains (Terumah 9), on the verse (Malachi 1:2), "I have loved you, says the LORD" - our Rabbis expounded: it was the generation of Malachi that He was speaking with, and they would answer Him. He says to them (ibid. 3:8), "shall a man rob God?" They answered Him: how have we robbed You? Rabbi Levi said: this is an Arabic expression - when one comes to argue with his fellow, he says to him, you have robbed me [gozlani]; and he says to him, you have wronged me [kov'ani] - "and you said, how have we robbed You?" [Wronged You] - through the tithes and terumah, which are not properly given. He returned and said to them: was not Esau Jacob's brother? And you said, how have You loved us? It is the way of the world that when a man has two sons, one the firstborn and one younger, who takes more? The firstborn. Esau came out first, as it is said (Genesis 25:25), "and the first came out red" - and it would have been fitting for him to take two portions - but I did not do so; rather, Jacob took two portions, this world and the World to Come, and Esau took only this world. See how I have loved you! From the earth to the firmament is a journey of five hundred years, and so from the firmament to the second [heaven], and from the second to the third, and from the third to the fourth, and from the fourth to the fifth, and from the fifth to the sixth, and from the sixth to the seventh - and there is no need to measure from the hooves of the Chayot - and the Throne is above them all. And see how much I held you dear, that I set all this aside and said to you, "make Me curtains of goats' hair," as it is said (Exodus 25:8), "and let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:5: Further, in Midrash Tanchuma (Kedoshim 5): out of the Holy One, blessed be He's love for Israel, He called them by His own name; in these words: "as the belt cleaves to the loins of a man, so have I made cleave to Me the whole house of Israel" (Jeremiah 13:11) - the Holy One, blessed be He, said: I am not like flesh and blood. Flesh and blood does not permit a commoner to be called by the king's name, but Israel are called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He - every beloved name by which the Holy One, blessed be He, is called, He called Israel by that name. He is called "Elohim," and He called Israel "Elohim," as it is said (Psalms 82:6), "I have said, you are gods [Elohim]." He is called "wise" [chacham], as it is said (Job 9:4), "wise of heart and mighty in strength," and He called Israel "wise," as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:6), "surely a wise and understanding people." He is called "David" [beloved], as it is said (Song of Songs 5:10), "my beloved [dodi] is radiant and ruddy," and He called Israel "beloved ones" [dodim], as it is said (Song of Songs 5:1), "eat, O friends, drink, and be drunk with love [dodim]." He is called "young man" [bachur], as it is said (ibid. 5:15), "his appearance is like Lebanon, choice [bachur] as the cedars," and He called Israel "chosen ones" [bachurim], as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:2), "and the LORD your God has chosen [bachar] you." He is called "pious" [chasid], as it is said (Jeremiah 3:12), "for I am pious, says the LORD," and He called Israel "pious," as it is said (Psalms 50:5), "gather to Me My pious ones." He is called "holy" [kadosh], and Israel are called "holy," as it is said (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I am holy." And even in the future to come, each and every one will be called "holy," as it is said (Isaiah 4:3), "and it shall come to pass, that he who is left in Zion, and he who remains in Jerusalem, shall be called holy" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:6: And along these lines, they say in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, page 121a): happy is Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to honor them above all the other peoples of the world. First He said to them (Exodus 19:6), "and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests" - He did not withhold His abundant love from them until He called them "a holy nation," which is greater; He did not withhold His love from them until He called them (Deuteronomy 7:6), "for you are a holy people"; He did not withhold His love from them until He called them (Exodus 22:30), "and you shall be holy men to Me," which is greater than all - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:7: Further, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Parashat Shemot, page 20a); he says there that everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created above, in the supernal realms, He created below, so that the worlds would be one unity. And he says afterward: He created the angels above; He created people in this world; He created the Leviathan in the sea - along the lines of (Exodus 36:18), "to couple the tent together, that it might be one." It is written of man (Genesis 9:6), "for in the image of God He made man," and it is written (Psalms 8:6), "and You have made him a little lower than the angels" - are people, then, precious in their deeds to this extent? And they are joined from a drop of a well, from which so many come to draw. And He chose among the supernal ones and He chose Israel; the supernal ones He did not call "children," but the lower ones He called "children" - this is what is written (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children of the LORD your God." He called them children, and they called Him "Father," as it is written (Isaiah 63:16), "for You are our Father"; and it is written (Song of Songs 2:16), "my beloved is mine, and I am his" - He chose me, and I chose Him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:8: And of this aspect it says in the Mishnah (Avot 3 [3:14]): beloved are Israel, for they are called children of the Omnipresent, as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children of the LORD your God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:9: Further, in the Midrash Yelammedenu, on the verse "you are children of the LORD your God" (Deuteronomy 14:1) - that the angels were called by five names of affection, and by all of them the Holy One, blessed be He, called Israel, holding them dearer than the ministering angels - copied in the Yalkut (Parashat Re'eh, section 891, page 278), on the verse "you are children," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:10: And further on there, Rashbi said: see in how many terms the Holy One, blessed be He, held Israel dear - He called them "children," and He returned and called them "a holy people" in this same passage, and three times He unified His Name upon them in this passage: "you are children of the LORD your God," "for you are a holy people to the LORD your God," and "and the LORD your God has chosen you" (14:1-2). The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: in this world I chose you and unified My Name upon you; in the future to come I will walk among you in My glory - "and I will walk among you" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:11: Further, concerning the matter of the Holy One, blessed be He's love, it says in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Rabbah, chapter 28) - and this is the end of the discourse we copied in chapter 1 of this Gate - in these words: this is what Scripture says (Song of Songs 8:7), "many waters cannot quench love" - the house of Israel, I am their surety in all the places of their dwelling, that they do not circumcise, nor recite Scripture, nor study Mishnah, except out of love for their Father in Heaven - for the Holy One, blessed be He, says to Israel: My children, I swear by My Throne of Glory that even if the idol-worshipping nations of the world were to stand and offer money, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:12: Further, concerning the matter of the Holy One, blessed be He's love for Israel, they say, of blessed memory, in Pesikta Rabbati (section 40), in these words: "put Me in remembrance, let us plead together" (Isaiah 43:26) - this is what Scripture says (ibid. 42:21), "the LORD desired, for His righteousness' sake," and so it says (ibid. 63:1), "I who speak in righteousness." The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I desire that you be found righteous in judgment. Come and see: when two enter into judgment, one silences his opponent and says, I go first, and his fellow does not let him, but says, I go first. But the Holy One, blessed be He, at the time He said to Israel, "come, let us plead together" - as it is written, "put Me in remembrance, let us plead together" - He said, who shall speak first? The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: you speak first - "declare, that you may be justified" (ibid. 43:26). Why? If I defeat you in judgment, it is I who lose; but if you defeat Me, I gain. I defeated the generation of the Flood - I lost all those multitudes: "and He blotted out all existence" (Genesis 7:23). Moses defeated Me: "and He said He would destroy them, had not Moses His chosen one" (Psalms 106:23) - I gained. This is what is written (Psalms 4:1), "for the leader [lamnatzeach], a psalm" - sing to the One who is defeated [being made to lose] and is glad - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:13: And in the Zohar (Parashat Balak, page 203b), they speak of a matter related to the previous discourse, concerning the love of the Holy One, blessed be He; in these words: he opened and said (Micah 6:5), "My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised" - "My people" - how merciful the Holy One, blessed be He, is toward His children! For even though they sin against Him, all His words are like a father toward his son: if the son sins against his father, he strikes him; and if striking him does not turn him from his way, he reproves him with words, and he does not accept it; the father says, I do not wish to do to my son what I have done until today - if I were to strike him, he would suffer in his head, and behold, his pain is with me too; if I rebuke him, behold, his appearance changes - what shall I do? Rather, I will go and plead with him and speak soft words to him, so that he not be grieved. So, in every manner, the Holy One, blessed be He, goes with Israel - He began to strike them, and they did not accept it. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I see with My children that because of the blows I struck them, their heads ached - woe, for from their pain I too ached, as it is written (Isaiah 63:9), "in all their affliction, He was afflicted"; I rebuked them, and their appearance changed, as it is written (Lamentations 4:8), "their appearance is darker than blackness; they are not recognized in the streets" - woe, when I look at them and they are not recognizable! Now I will plead with them in supplications: "My people, what have I done to you, and how have I wearied you? My unique child, beloved of My soul, what have I done to you? I gave you dominion over all the members of My Heichal, I gave you dominion over all the kings of the worlds; and if I did other deeds to you, testify against Me - you be a witness for Me. My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam son of Beor answered him" - "remember now" - please remember what he devised - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:14: And along these lines, it says in Midrash Tanchuma, on the verse (Numbers 23:8), "how shall I curse whom God has not cursed?" - in these words: at the time they were fit to be cursed, they were not cursed - but rather, at the time Jacob entered to receive the blessings, as it is written (Genesis 27:16), "and the skins of the kids of the goats," and so on, his father said to him, who are you? He said to him, I am Esau your firstborn - one who brings forth falsehood from his mouth is not fit to be cursed, and not only that, but he was blessed, as it is said, "he shall also be blessed" - and how can I curse him? This is "God has not cursed."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:15: Another interpretation: it is the way of the world that a legion that rebels against the king has [forfeited its right to] life; but even though they [Israel] denied and rebelled against Him and said, "these are your gods, O Israel," they were not fit for destruction - even at that hour His affection did not budge from them, but rather He accompanied them with the clouds of glory, the manna, and the well - and so it says (Nehemiah 9:18), "even when they made themselves a molten calf," and so on, "yet You, in Your abundant mercies, did not forsake them," and so on, "and You withheld not Your manna from their mouth" - and how could I curse them?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:16: At the time He commands them concerning the blessings and the curses - for the blessings, He mentions them, as it is said (Deuteronomy 27:12), "these shall stand to bless the people"; but for the curses, He did not press them, as it is said (ibid. 27:13), "and these shall stand for the curse." And further, when they sin and He speaks of bringing a curse upon them, it is not written that He brings them, but for the blessings He Himself blesses them - as it says (ibid. 28:1), "and it shall come to pass, if you shall diligently hearken... and the LORD your God will set you on high" - "the LORD will command the blessing to be with you" (28:8) - but for the curses it is written (ibid. 28:15), "and it shall come to pass, if you will not hearken... that all these curses shall come upon you" - of themselves. Behold, "how shall I curse whom God has not cursed?" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:17: And since we see that the Holy One, blessed be He, desires Israel's blessing and their praise, a person must always teach in their defense, and never for the prosecution. And so it says in the Yelammedenu, concerning the matter of Gideon: when it was said to him (Judges 6:14), "go in this your strength" - Rabbi Yehuda bar Shalom said, it was the night of Passover, that night when it was said to him (ibid. 6:13), "and where are all His wondrous works" - where are the wonders that God did for our fathers on this night, when He struck the firstborn of Egypt and brought Israel out from there rejoicing? And since he taught in Israel's defense, the Holy One, blessed be He, said, it is right that I reveal Myself to him in My glory - as it is said, "and the LORD turned to him and said, go in this your strength" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: you have the strength to teach in Israel's defense - by your merit they shall be redeemed, as it is said, "and you shall save Israel" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:18: Further, in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Zuta, chapter 8), on the verse (I Kings 19:9), "what are you doing here, Elijah?" - in these words: "what are you doing here, Elijah?" - he should have said before Him: Master of the universe, Your children are the children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who performed Your will in Your world. He did not do so, but rather said, "I have been very jealous," and so on. The Holy One, blessed be He, began to speak with him words of comfort; He said, when I descended to give the Torah to Israel, none but the ministering angels descended with Me, who wished them well - as it is said (ibid. 19:12), "go and stand on the mountain," and so on, "and after the earthquake, a fire" - He waited for him three hours, but he still stood on his original words and said, "I have been very jealous." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him (ibid. 19:16), "and Elisha son of Shafat shall you anoint as prophet in your place" - what you have in mind, you are unable to accomplish. He said to him: forever [are] you zealous - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:19: Further, out of the Holy One, blessed be He's love, He makes His Shechinah dwell with them even in exile - as they elaborate in the Zohar, Parashat Bechukotai (page 115b), on the verse (Leviticus 26:44), "and yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them" - and He is called "saved" [nosha] in their redemption, as it is said (Zechariah 9:9), "righteous and saved," and so on - as they elaborate in Midrash Tanchuma, end of Parashat Acharei Mot (section 12).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:20: Further, they say in the Midrash (on Proverbs), "in the multitude of people is the king's glory" (Proverbs 14:28) - Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said, to tell the praise and greatness of the Holy One, blessed be He - that although He has a thousand thousand thousands and myriad myriads of companies of ministering angels who serve Him and praise Him, He desires only the praise of Israel, as it is said, "in the multitude of people is the king's glory" - and "people" [am] refers only to Israel, as it is said (Isaiah 43:21), "this people I have formed for Myself" - why? So that they may recount My praise. And so it says (Psalms 47:10), "the princes of the peoples are gathered together, the people of the God of Abraham." Rabbi Simon said: the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted in His world at the time Israel gather in synagogues and study houses and give praise, thanksgiving, and greatness to the Holy One, blessed be He. And Rabbi Yishmael said: at that hour, when they hear an exposition [aggadah] from the mouth of a sage, and afterward answer "amen, yehei shmei rabba" - at that hour the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices and says to the ministering angels: come and see the people I formed for Myself, how they praise Me! At that hour they clothe [Him] in majesty and splendor - therefore it says, "in the multitude of people is the king's glory," but "in the lack of people is the prince's ruin" (ibid.) - if they cease from words of Torah, I too will cease from them the proofs of the Torah - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:21: And of the matter that arouses, a person should remember how many miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for us, showing His love for us - first, at the Exodus from Egypt, concerning the matter of the plagues, which were specifically for Egypt: behold, the plague of blood - it was blood for Egypt and water for Israel; and along these lines, in the plague of pestilence (Exodus 9:4), "and the LORD shall make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, and nothing shall die of all that belongs to the children of Israel." Third, in the plague of darkness (ibid. 10:23), "but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings" - in every place the Israelite went, the light went with him, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Shemot Rabbah 14:3). Further, in the plague of the firstborn (ibid. 11:7), "but against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog sharpen his tongue." And what He commanded concerning the giving of the blood - the matter was like a kind of segulah [talisman], hinting at the three yuds, which is mercy, and He said (Exodus 12:23), "and will not allow the destroyer to come in."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:22: And so Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, rebuked Israel in Deuteronomy (Deuteronomy 4:34), "or has any god ever attempted to go and take for himself a nation from the midst of a nation, by trials, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand, and by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, according to all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes" - and our Sages, of blessed memory, say in the Midrash on the passage of the manna (Yalkut, section 258) that it is written (Exodus 16:6), "and you shall know that the LORD has brought you out of the land of Egypt" - they say, from here you learn that the Exodus from Egypt is equal in weight to all the miracles and mighty acts the Omnipresent performed for Israel - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:23: Further, they say in Bamidbar Rabbah, on the verse (Numbers 14:27), "how long shall I bear with this evil congregation" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said: as it were, a person who acquires a servant, the servant takes the lantern and lights the way for the one who acquired him; but I did not do so - rather, you are My servants (cf. Leviticus 25:55), "for the children of Israel are servants to Me," and I take the lantern and light the way for you - to this point. And the explanation of "lantern" is a metaphor for the pillar of fire that lit the way for them at night. And in truth, the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night correspond to the measure of day and the measure of night, and their partners are Chesed and Din, and both together are YHVH-Elohim - and this indicates the strength of His love for us, blessed be He, and those who hold to the plain sense alone, who do not know the inner secret of the Torah, do not perceive this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:24: And it further says there: another interpretation - it is the way of the world that when a person acquires a servant, if he goes on a journey, his servant goes before him and prepares his lodging [itimasia]; but I did not do so - rather, you are My servants, and I prepared your lodging, as it is said (Numbers 10:33), "and the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD," and so on, "to seek out a resting place for them."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:25: Another interpretation: it is the way of the world that when a person acquires a servant, his servant bakes bread for him; but I did not do so - you are My servants, and I baked bread for you from heaven, as it is said (Psalms 78:25), "man ate the bread of the mighty."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:26: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses, "let Me consume them" (cf. Exodus 32:10, adapted). He said before Him: Master of the universe, You are slow to anger! And a servant - if his deeds are good and he listens to his master, and his master looks upon him with a favorable countenance, one does not credit the master with kindness; but when do they credit him? When the servant is of bad character, and his master [still] looks upon him with a favorable countenance. So You too, do not look upon the stiffness of their neck, as it is said (Deuteronomy 9:27), "do not look upon the stubbornness of this people." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: for your sake I will forgive them, as it is said (Numbers 14:20), "and the LORD said, I have forgiven, according to your word" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:27: And close to this, it explains there that everything a father is obligated to his son, the Holy One, blessed be He, did for Israel - a father is obligated to redeem him, to teach him Torah, to anoint him and clothe him - all these He did for Israel; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:28: They say in the Midrash (Midrash Shloshah VeArba'ah, section 58; Tanchuma, Beshalach 10), on the verse (Exodus 14:16), "and you, lift up your rod," concerning the splitting of the Red Sea, that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say ten miracles were performed with it; in these words: ten miracles were performed for Israel at the Sea. The waters split and became like a kind of dome, as it is said (Habakkuk 3:14), "You pierced with his own staves"; it was divided into two, as it is said (Exodus 14:26), "stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it"; it became dry land, as it is said (ibid. 14:29), "and the children of Israel walked upon dry land"; it became like a kind of clay, as it is said (Habakkuk 3:15), "You walked through the sea with Your horses, through the mud of great waters"; it became crumbs upon crumbs, as it is said (Psalms 74:13), "You broke the sea in pieces by Your strength"; it became rocks upon rocks, as it is said (ibid.), "You broke the heads of the sea monsters upon the waters"; it became pieces upon pieces, as it is said (ibid. 136:13), "to Him who divided the Red Sea into parts"; it became heaps upon heaps, as it is said (Exodus 15:8), "and with the blast of Your nostrils the waters were piled up"; it became like a mound, as it is said (ibid.), "the floods stood upright like a heap"; sweet water came forth for them from within salty water, as it is said (Psalms 78:16), "and He brought streams also out of the rock"; the sea froze into two parts and became like a kind of crystal glass, as it is said (Exodus, ibid.), "the deeps congealed in the heart of the sea" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:29: Further, to consider and discern the miracle performed for them at the Jordan, upon their entry into the Land - our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say there (Sotah 34b; Yalkut Yehoshua, section 14) how wide the waters were: twelve miles by twelve miles, corresponding to the camp of Israel. Rabbi Elazar said to Rabbi Shimon: according to your words, is a man swift, or is water swift? You must say water is swift - if so, the water would come and wash them away! Rather, this teaches that the waters were piled up, dome upon dome, more than three hundred miles, until all the kings of east and west saw them, as it is said (Joshua 5:1), "and it came to pass, when [they] heard," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:30: Further, in recounting the miracle, it says further on (Yalkut): our Rabbis taught, once the last of Israel came up from the Jordan, the waters returned to their place, as it is said (ibid. 4:18), "and it came to pass, when the priests who bore the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD came up out of the midst of the Jordan," and so on. It follows that the Ark and its bearers were on one side, and Israel on another; the Ark carried its bearers and crossed over, as it is said (ibid. 4:11), "and it came to pass, when all the people had completely crossed over, that the Ark of the LORD crossed over, and the priests, before the people." And for this matter Uzzah was punished, as it is said (II Samuel 6:6), "and Uzzah put out his hand to the Ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled; and the LORD's anger was kindled against Uzzah" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Uzzah, it carries its bearers - does it not carry itself, all the more so? To this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:31: And our Rabbis, peace be upon them, instituted for us the blessing "by whose word all things came to be" and "who creates many souls" over drinking water, so that we remember the miracles performed for us concerning water - and this is proven in Devarim Rabbah, Parashat Eikev, in these words: (Deuteronomy 9:1), "hear, O Israel, you are to cross over the Jordan today" - it happened that an Israelite drinking water for his thirst says, "blessed is He by whose word all things came to be." Rabbi Tarfon says, "who creates many souls and their deficiencies." The Rabbis say: come and see, all the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for Israel, He performed only concerning water. How so? While they were still in Egypt, He performed miracles for them with the Nile - Rabbi Yitzchak said, the Egyptians and Israelites would go to drink water from the river; the Egyptian would drink blood and the Israelite would drink water. And when they left Egypt, the Holy One, blessed be He, performed miracles only concerning water - from where? As it is said (Psalms 114:3), "the sea saw, and fled" - what did it see? Rabbi Nehorai said, the Explicit Name was engraved on the staff, and it [the sea] was split, as it is said (Psalms 77:17), "the waters saw You, they were afraid." They came to Marah when they came up from the sea, and the waters were bitter - He performed miracles for them there - from where? As it is said (Exodus 15:25), "and the LORD showed him a tree," and so on. At the rock, He performed miracles for them with water, as it is said (Numbers 20:8), "and you shall speak to the rock," and so on. At the well, He performed miracles for them and they said a song, as it is said (ibid. 21:17), "then Israel sang this song." Moses said to them: know that all the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for you were performed only concerning water - even when you cross the Jordan to inherit the Land, He is destined to perform miracles for you with the waters of the Jordan - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:32: And what should be examined precisely in this discourse is simple: what connection is there between beginning "an Israelite drinking water for his thirst" and the verse "hear, O Israel"? And the connection [with] "the Rabbis say, come and see all the miracles He performed" to the preceding blessings, particularly "who creates many souls"?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:33: Rather, the matter is that the author of the discourse sensed a difficulty in the verse: what does Moses come to teach us by saying "you are to cross over the Jordan today"? And the intent in resolving this difficulty is in what he says at the end of the discourse - that the intent is that the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to perform miracles for them with the waters of the Jordan - and in order to explain this matter, he was compelled to preface this whole introduction.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:34: And he says, "an Israelite drinking water for his thirst blesses 'shehakol'" - and this is, as it were, informing us and hinting to us the reason why they instituted this blessing over water in this formula, "by whose word all things came to be," and did not specify the water in it as in the case of other blessings, "who creates the fruit of the tree" - and it would have been fitting to say that He created the water. And further, Rabbi Tarfon says, "who creates many souls and their deficiencies" - why does Rabbi Tarfon inform us of this matter concerning water more than other things? And according to the law, anything whose blessing begins with "shehakol," such as things that do not grow from the ground, ends with the blessing "many souls" - and further, the formula of the blessing "who creates many souls and their deficiencies" is a comprehensive blessing, as the Tur writes, Orach Chaim, section 207, that the explanation of "who creates many souls and their deficiencies" is "and all that they lack" - and Rabbeinu Yonah writes that it is a term related to "all your lack is upon Me" - meaning "need" - and concerning all the other things He created in the world, which are only for pleasure, "to give life to the soul of every living thing, blessed be the Life of the worlds" - concerning everything He created, this is attached to the end of the blessing. If so, let us return to our difficulty: since this blessing is a comprehensive one, why is its specific application to water mentioned?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:35: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, intended to resolve these two difficulties, and they say, the Rabbis say, come and see, all the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for Israel, He performed only concerning water. And one must be precise about these words, for it is impossible in any way to understand them literally - for several miracles were performed for Israel that were not concerning water: in Egypt, of the eight plagues [before blood and hail], only the plague of blood and the plague of hail had any connection to water; and afterward, the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night, and the giving of the manna and the quail, and the giving of the Torah in fire, and the war against Amalek, and the war against Sichon and Og, and several miracles that Elijah and Elisha performed - none of these were concerning water. How so?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:36: Rather, without doubt the intent is that all the miracles performed were performed only from the side of plain Chesed, and they compared them to water, for water is the sustaining of the world - this is what is written (Psalms 104:3), "who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters," and it is written (ibid. 89:3), "I have said, the world is built with kindness" - and therefore the world cannot exist without water.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:37: And therefore he brought all these miracles that were performed concerning water, for all the miracles themselves indicate the side of Chesed. How so? At the Nile, the Israelite drank water and the Egyptian drank blood - behold, the side of Chesed; and because it was bound with Gevurah, it was blood for the Egyptian - and the rest of the distinctions are clear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:38: And it says at the end of the discourse, "even when you cross the Jordan" - so that you not say that the attribute of Chesed was used only until their arrival in the Land. And there is further proof in Vayikra Rabbah, Parashat "Uneta'tem Kol Etz Ma'achal" (Leviticus 19:23); see there. To this it informs us that even as they cross the Jordan to inherit the Land, the side of Chesed is what accompanies them there - and this is what the verse says (Deuteronomy 9:1), "you [attah] are to cross over the Jordan today" - for the word "attah" is superfluous, since it already said "hear, O Israel," and further, it would have been fitting to say "you [plural] are crossing" - rather, the intent is toward the attribute of Chesed, called "Attah," as in (Psalms 110:4), "You [Attah] are a priest forever" - He is the One who crosses the Jordan with you, to perform a miracle for you with the waters of the Jordan.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:39: And the reason that miracles are related to Chesed is that a miracle is a change of nature, and "hateva" [nature] adds up in numerical value to "Elohim" - and behold, the attribute of Gevurah, which is Elohim, employs the lower attribute of Elohim [nature]; and the creation of the world was through judgment: "in the beginning God [Elohim] created" (Genesis 1:1), "yes, My hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand has spanned the heavens" (Isaiah 48:13) - it follows that the change of nature is from the side of Chesed and mercy, and the attribute of the righteous one [Tzaddik, i.e., Yesod] is called "nes" [miracle] - and so it is explained in the Tikkunim. And it seems to me, because its secret is that "kol" [all] is "in heaven and on earth," and it adds up to 110, equal in numerical value to "Mah" and "Adonai" - and this unification is from the side of Chesed, namely Al-oo-Ah [an anagram/spelling of Eloah as El-Vav-Heh], as explained in Parashat Vayikra (23b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:40: And behold, with this introduction, we may understand these blessings our Rabbis, of blessed memory, instituted over water. The reason it says "by whose word [bidvaro] all things came to be" is that "everything" - meaning all the miracles performed for us - "came to be by His word," which is Chesed. And it says "hakol" [everything/all], for the miracles are from the attribute of "Kol" [All, i.e., Yesod], "Kol" that passes over the commandments [an allusion to the covenant]. And they say "hakol" is in the heh, to hint at "kol heh," as explained there in the Tikkunim. And all the miracles are performed through the bond of the miracle with Chesed - and this is "came to be by His word."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 7:41: And there is no difficulty with the word "his word" [devaro] being related to Chesed, for we already find the term "davar" and "devaro" related to Chesed, as it says (Psalms 107:20), "He sent His word and healed them," and likewise (ibid. 130:5), "I wait for the LORD, my soul waits, and for His word I hope"; "He sends out His word and melts them" (ibid. 147:18) - and the melting of the snows is from the side of Chesed, as explained in Parashat Bereshit (29b). And likewise, "would that God spoke" [Mi yiten Eloah daber] (Job 11:5); "for God speaks in one way" (ibid. 33:14); (Psalms 85:9), "I will hear what God the LORD will speak, for He will speak peace." And likewise speech is compared to water, as it says (Proverbs 18:4), "the words of a man's mouth are deep waters." "The opening of Your words gives light" (Psalms 119:130) - and "gives light" [ya'ir] is Chesed, certainly light.
